step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture diagram represents a streaming data management pipeline with four primary functional blocks: Ingestion, Aggregation + Machine Learning (AGG+ML), Profile, and Serving, alongside central storage/streaming layers (S3, Kafka).

Nodes:
1. Ingestion ECS (ECS) in the INGESTION block.
2. S3 Bucket (S3) at the top.
3. Kafka (MSK) streaming backbone at the top.
4. AGG+ML EMR (EMR) inside AGG+ML block.
5. AGG+ML ECS (ECS) inside AGG+ML block.
6. Couchbase Database (CouchBase) under AGG+ML.
7. Profile ECS (ECS) inside PROFILE block.
8. Couchbase/Elasticsearch Database (CouchBase) under PROFILE.
9. Serving ECS (ECS) inside SERVING block.
10. Serving Couchbase Database (CouchBase) under SERVING.

Edges:
- Ingestion ECS connects to S3 and Kafka.
- EMR connects to S3.
- Kafka feeds AGG+ML ECS, and AGG+ML ECS outputs back to Kafka and writes to Couchbase.
- Kafka feeds Profile ECS, Profile ECS writes to CB/ES and sends audience data back to Kafka.
- Kafka feeds Serving ECS, which writes to Serving Couchbase.

nodes.name: Ingestion ECS
nodes.notes: Cleans and prepares event stream data

nodes.name: AGG+ML EMR
nodes.notes: Batch data aggregation and ML computations

nodes.name: Serving ECS
nodes.notes: Serves user profile and audience queries

edges.notes: Ingestion writes raw/cleaned event logs to S3
EMR reads/writes historical files from/to S3
Kafka streams events to AGG+ML ECS
AGG+ML ECS stores state in Couchbase
AGG+ML outputs user attributes to Kafka
Kafka streams user attributes to Profile ECS
Profile ECS stores combined user profiles in CB/ES
Profile ECS publishes audience data to Kafka
Kafka streams audience membership to Serving ECS
Serving ECS indexes audience membership in Couchbase
